title: Cancellation parameters must be read from the Pause contract's logs, never from the Spell being cancelled
content:
A.1.10.5.3.1.3.6 gives an explicit sourcing rule for the four parameters Protego needs to identify a planned action: they "should always be determined by inspecting the logs emitted from the `plot` function of the Pause contract. The parameters should never be determined by calling functions on the Spell to be canceled, because these functions may not return the correct values in the case of a malicious Spell."

This is a small clause carrying a large security principle: **do not let the adversary supply its own identifiers.** A Spell exposes convenient accessors describing what it will do, and reading them is the obvious way to construct a cancellation call. But a hostile Spell controls those return values, so it can present one identity to anyone trying to cancel it and execute another — defeating the drop while appearing cancellable.

The Pause contract's `plot` event is the correct source because it was emitted by the *scheduling* system at the moment the action was queued. It is a record written by the trusted component about the untrusted one, and it cannot be retroactively edited by the Spell it describes.

Generalized: when verifying or revoking something potentially hostile, authoritative data must come from the infrastructure that recorded the event, not from the object under suspicion. The same reasoning is why A.1.10.5.3.2.2.1 requires an independent party to attest that an Emergency Drop Spell is authentic instead of trusting the artifact's self-description.
description: A malicious Spell's own getter functions may return false values, so Protego callers derive usr, tag, fax and eta from the plot event emitted when the action was scheduled.
